difference_if_any: The masses are fractional, and the erase strengths (rho*y_j, rho*x_i) depend on the state rather than only the input. That makes the recursion quadratic in C and produces order-dependent 2x2 cross-ratios, which are a signature of the soft relaxation. The other differences are value-side exclusivity (the column erase) and a fallback that routes an unbound key's mass to unbound values. None of these is a new learning rule: training is ordinary BPTT on type-level rates and a background.
family_why: In its trained regime the state is a one-hot key->value table with overwrite on both key and value side (bidirectional map with forcePut), an LRU-ordered capacity cap, and a readout that returns the stored value for the query key or backs off to unbound values. The fractional, state-gated erase strengths are a soft relaxation of that table, not a different form.
mapping: Token i is a one-hot key slot (row i) and token j is a value slot (column j). C is a soft, P_max-capped key->value table. On pair (i,j), step 4 does three things. (1) Row i: entries l != j are scaled by (1 - beta_r) with beta_r = rho*y_j. This is exactly one row of a one-hot delta rule, S_i <- S_i + beta_r (e_j - S_i), which on its own would add beta_r(1 - C_ij) = rho*y_j*(x_i + row_i) to C_ij. (2) Column j: entries m != i are scaled by (1 - beta_c) with beta_c = rho*x_i. This is the same delta rule applied to C^T (value -> key), which on its own would add rho*x_i*(y_j + col_j). (3) The card's increment rho(x_i y_j + x_i col_j + y_j row_i) equals the sum of the two delta increments minus one copy of rho*x_i*y_j. So the update is a two-sided (row and column) one-hot delta rule whose erase strengths are gated by the free masses x_i = 1 - rowsum_i and y_j = 1 - colsum_j, read from the state. In the regime the card trains to and states every capability in (rho >= 0.95, A1), the table is a near-binary partial matching. A write (i,j) inserts i->j and evicts the previous partner of i and of j. This is the textbook bidirectional map with forcePut (two hash maps kept mutually consistent), with one difference: when both i and j are already committed, x_i and y_j are about 0 and the write is a near no-op. Records sit in last-write order with min-concentration/oldest eviction at P_max (an LRU-style cap). The readout returns the stored value for the query key; if the key is unbound, it backs off to a background u restricted to still-unbound values (y + eta). That is an exact-match cache readout with a matching-aware fallback.
textbook_why: The update is one explicit Euler step of textbook mass-action kinetics for bimolecular binding plus the two strand-exchange (displacement) reactions under stoichiometric conservation, with rho playing k*dt. The losses rho*x_i*C_mj and rho*y_j*C_il and the gain rho(x_i y_j + x_i col_j + y_j row_i) are exactly those Euler terms. The card changes only scheduling (fire on adjacent token pairs, with a gate), rate parameterization (saturating low-rank prior), species capping (from the reduced-mechanism reference), and adds a readout. The reaction law itself is unchanged.
why: The broken_invariant holds. Step 4 rescales cells outside (i,j), and its increment depends on the state. A per-cell-kernel Sinkhorn readout fixes 2x2 cross-ratios from the four cells' own histories, and the toy example shows A and B differ, so the parent's Sinkhorn/count-cache mapping cannot be repaired. why_unrepairable is also right that a single input-gated one-hot delta rule touches only row i and is linear in S. The repair that came closest is two coupled one-hot delta rules, one on C and one on C^T, with erase gates read from row and column sums. It reproduces the update up to a single -rho*x_i*y_j correction at (i,j). In the hard limit the card itself operates in (rho >= 0.95), that construction is a bidirectional map with forcePut semantics, an LRU-style cap, and an exact-match lookup plus a fallback over unmatched values. Every capability claim (one-shot recall, overwrite, ownership transfer, elimination, oldest-first eviction, filler invariance) is a property of that data structure. The only claim that needs the fractional dynamics is the cross-ratio order dependence, which is an artifact of the relaxation, not a capability. So the card escapes the parent's family but lands on a soft bimap cache with chemistry names. It is not radical. History: this is the same lens as card-8dc4db49 and card-d694c9fe, which died as a count cache and Sinkhorn/IPF respectively, and card-f37de377. This card does change the named equation, replacing accumulation and equilibrium with displacement kinetics, so it does not repeat their exact failure. It falls into the neighbouring cache family instead.
